reasons.A: Closest movement: long semicolon-and-dash sentences broken by short turns, stacked questions, second-person address and a dry ironic glance at the writers, all at the passage's own density.
reasons.B: Right period register and rhetorical questions, but the sentences run on in even and-chains with less variation, and 'robustious' and the extended battlefield figure lay the manner on a little thick.
reasons.C: Plain modern first-person prose in short declarative sentences with no semicolons or dashes and no irony; the rhythm and diction are far from the passage.
